The thumb swells under the finger, the track stretches like rubber past either end and springs back with the release velocity, a value tag hangs off the thumb and sways with its speed, and marks act as detents the thumb clicks into. Arrows, Shift+arrows, PageUp, PageDown, Home, and End work as in a native range input.

members.name: label
members.doc: Visible label; it also names the thumb.

members.name: onValueCommit
members.doc: Runs once a drag is released or a key changes the value.

members.name: largeStep
members.doc: PageUp, PageDown, and Shift with an arrow move this far. Defaults to a tenth of the range.

members.name: marks
members.doc: Detents. A dragged thumb clicks into each one and holds for a few pixels before letting go. Labels print under the track.

members.name: format
members.doc: Formats the readout, the bubble, and the spoken value.

members.name: showValue
members.doc: Show the value beside the label. The bubble over the thumb still appears while dragging or using keys.

members.name: startIcon
members.doc: Icons at either end. The one on the side being pulled past its limit is pushed outward with the track.

members.name: name
members.doc: Submits the value with a form.

components.name: RangeHistogramSlider
components.doc: A two thumb range over a histogram of the data it filters. Bars inside the range light up, cut exactly at each thumb on the frame it moves; the thumbs follow the pointer 1:1, never cross, rubber-band at the ends, and settle on bar edges with the release velocity. A press anywhere on the histogram or track springs the nearest thumb there. Arrows step, Shift+arrows and PageUp or PageDown move one bar, and Home or End go to a thumb's limit.

members.name: label
members.doc: Visible label. The thumbs are named from it unless `thumbLabels` says otherwise.

members.name: data
members.doc: The raw values the histogram counts, such as every listing's price.

members.name: onValueCommit
members.doc: Runs once a drag is released or a key changes the value.

members.name: min
members.doc: Defaults to the smallest and largest data values.

members.name: bins
members.doc: How many bars the histogram draws.

members.name: snapToBins
members.doc: A released thumb that lands near the edge of a bar settles on that edge, so a range never cuts a bar in half.

members.name: minStepsBetweenThumbs
members.doc: The closest the two thumbs may sit, in steps.

members.name: format
members.doc: Formats the readout and the spoken values.

members.name: name
members.doc: Submits the range with a form, one hidden input per thumb.

components.name: RulerSlider
components.doc: A precise value input shaped like a tape measure. A ruler of ticks slides under a fixed needle: drag it 1:1, flick it and it coasts with momentum onto a tick, pull it past either end and it rubber-bands back, or tap a spot to glide it there. The readout rolls each digit as the tape passes. Arrows step one tick, Shift+arrows and PageUp or PageDown move one labelled tick, Home and End go to the ends, and horizontal trackpad scrolling moves the tape.

members.name: label
members.doc: Visible label; it also names the control.

members.name: onValueCommit
members.doc: Runs once the tape comes to rest after a drag, a flick, a tap, or a key.

members.name: step
members.doc: The value of one small tick. The tape always rests on a tick.

members.name: largeStep
members.doc: PageUp, PageDown, and Shift with an arrow move this far. Defaults to one labelled tick.

members.name: majorEvery
members.doc: Small ticks between labelled ticks.

members.name: spacing
members.doc: Pixels between small ticks. Wider spacing gives finer control.

members.name: format
members.doc: Formats the readout, the tick labels, and the spoken value.

members.name: unit
members.doc: Unit shown after the readout and spoken with the value, such as "cm".

members.name: name
members.doc: Submits the value with a form.

types.name: InlineEditProps
types.doc: Click-to-edit text for names and short fields that are read far more often than they change, such as a project name or its description. The text turns into a field in place with the same metrics, so nothing around it moves, and the box grows with what you type. Enter saves optimistically and a check draws once the save lands; Escape rolls the text back. A failed save restores the last saved value and says why. Use a regular form when several fields must be saved together.

members.name: value
members.doc: The saved value. A new value from outside replaces the text while it is not being edited.

members.name: onSave
members.doc: Persists the new value. Return a promise to show the saving state, and reject it to roll back.

members.name: label
members.doc: Accessible name, for example “Project name”.

members.name: validate
members.doc: Returns a message when the draft cannot be saved.

members.name: placeholder
members.doc: Shown when the value is empty.

members.name: multiline
members.doc: Wraps onto several lines and grows in height. Enter still saves; Shift+Enter adds a line break.

members.name: variant
members.doc: `title` for names and headings, `body` for descriptions.

members.name: as
members.doc: The element that holds the text, so a title can stay a heading.

defaults.emptyHint: "Try a shorter word or check the spelling."

members.name: meta
members.doc: One short line under the title, such as the type, owner, or last edit.

members.name: group
members.doc: Results gather under this heading, in the order groups first appear in `items`.

members.name: keywords
members.doc: Extra words that should also find this item.

types.name: ExpandingSearchProps
types.doc: A search that waits as an icon button until it is needed. Use it in headers and toolbars where a full field would crowd the layout. The button morphs into the field, results unfold beneath it, and Escape, choosing a result, or leaving the field empty folds it back into the icon. Place it in the space the field may grow into; it fills that space's width and keeps the button on the `anchor` edge.

members.name: label
members.doc: Names the button, the field, and the results, such as "Search projects and docs".

members.name: suggestions
members.doc: Shown before anything is typed, such as recent searches.

members.name: expandedWidth
members.doc: The widest the field grows. It never grows past its container.

members.name: anchor
members.doc: The edge the button sits on; the field grows away from it.

members.name: emptyHint
members.doc: A short tip under the empty state.

types.name: ChipGroupProps
types.doc: Selectable filter chips for narrowing a list by facets people toggle often, such as topics, statuses, or tags. Selecting morphs the chip: a check grows in, the label slides over, and the chip's edge follows on a spring while its neighbours glide to their new places, even across lines. Long sets fold behind a “+N more” chip that opens with a height morph. Arrow keys move between chips, Space or Enter toggles, and each chip is a pressed or unpressed button.

members.name: label
members.doc: Accessible name of the group, such as “Topics”.

members.name: multiple
members.doc: Allow several chips at once. In single mode the selected chip can still be cleared.

members.name: maxVisible
members.doc: Chips shown before the rest fold behind a “+N more” chip. Chips selected when it folds stay in view.

members.name: remaining
members.doc: Characters still missing. Shown as a rolling count beside the rule while it is unmet.

members.name: short
members.doc: True while the password is shorter than the short length, so the meter holds at its first step.

types.name: PasswordStrengthLevels
types.doc: The strength words, one per meter step. Override them to translate the meter.

types.name: PasswordStrengthMessages
types.doc: Every user-facing string in PasswordStrength. All have English defaults; pass only the ones you change.

members.name: showPassword
members.doc: Name of the show password toggle. It is a pressed toggle (aria-pressed), so the name stays the same in both states.

members.name: meterLabel
members.doc: Accessible name of the strength meter.

members.name: noPassword
members.doc: Meter value text while the field is empty.

members.name: rulesLabel
members.doc: Accessible name of the requirements list.

members.name: ruleMet
members.doc: Read after a rule's label for screen readers, including any leading punctuation.

members.name: remainingPrefix
members.doc: Words around the rolling count beside an unmet rule, as in "4 more".

members.name: summary
members.type: (result: { label: string; met: number; total: number }) => string
members.doc: The polite live-region summary read after each change.

types.name: PasswordStrengthMessagesInput
types.doc: Partial messages, with partial strength words, for the `messages` prop.

types.name: PasswordStrengthProps
types.doc: A new password field that shows how strong the password is while it is typed: four segments fill and change tone, each rule checks off with a drawn tick, and the strength word morphs in place. Use it when creating or changing a password; use a plain password field for sign in. Scoring happens on the device, nothing is sent anywhere.

members.name: rules
members.doc: Rules to check. Strength is the share of rules met, spread over four steps.

members.name: error
members.doc: Error copy tied to the field. The field shakes once each time a new error appears.

members.name: messages
members.doc: Translated or reworded copy. Every string has an English default; see PasswordStrengthMessages.

members.name: shortLength
members.doc: Below this many characters the meter holds at its first step and reads "Too short". Defaults to 8.

members.name: countCharacters
members.doc: How characters are counted for shortLength. Defaults to code points, so an emoji counts once; pass `password => password.length` to count UTF-16 units like a server might.

types.name: PasswordRuleLabels
types.doc: Labels for the built-in rules. `length` receives the minimum length.

members.name: minLength
members.doc: Characters the length rule asks for. Defaults to 12.

members.name: labels
members.doc: Translated or reworded rule labels.

members.name: countCharacters
members.doc: How the length rule counts characters. Defaults to code points.

members.name: shortLength
members.doc: Below this many characters a password stays at the first step, however varied it is. Defaults to 8.

members.name: levels
members.doc: Strength words for the result's label.

members.name: countCharacters
members.doc: How characters are counted for shortLength. Defaults to code points.

types.name: BottomSheetProps
types.doc: A sheet that rises from the bottom edge and rests at one or more heights (detents). Use it for secondary tasks where a peek is useful before committing to the full view: trip details, share options, filters. Use a dialog when the decision must interrupt, and a drawer for side panels on wide layouts.

members.name: trigger
members.doc: The control that opens the sheet, usually a button. Focus returns to it when the sheet closes.

members.name: detents
members.doc: Resting heights as fractions of the viewport height. The sheet opens at `initialDetent` and never grows past the largest.

members.name: initialDetent
members.doc: Index into the sorted detents the sheet opens at. Defaults to the smallest.

members.name: container
members.doc: Renders the sheet inside this element instead of the page body: it rises from the element's bottom edge, the detents become fractions of the element's height and the dim covers only the element. The element needs position: relative and overflow: hidden. The page around it stays usable while the sheet is open: nothing is scroll-locked or hidden from assistive technology.

members.name: onOpenAutoFocus
members.doc: Runs when the sheet opens, before it moves focus to itself. Call `event.preventDefault()` to leave focus where it is.

types.name: HoverCardProps
types.doc: A rich preview of a person or link that opens after a short hover or keyboard focus, for mentions, avatars, and references where a click should stay free for navigation. It waits half a second, opens almost at once when moving between triggers, stays open while the pointer travels into it, and closes fast on leave or Escape. On touch, a tap toggles it. Keep the content read only; anything actionable belongs behind the trigger itself.

members.name: children
members.doc: The trigger, such as a mention button or a link. It must accept a ref and be focusable.

members.name: content
members.doc: The preview. `HoverCardProfile` covers people; any read only content works.

members.name: openDelay
members.doc: Milliseconds of hover before the first card opens.

members.name: closeDelay
members.doc: Milliseconds of grace after the pointer leaves, so it can travel into the card.

members.name: container
members.doc: Render the card inside this element and limit collisions to it (used by the demo stages).

members.name: defaultOpen
members.doc: Starts with the card open, for previews. It then behaves as usual: leaving the trigger and card, Escape, or a press elsewhere closes it.

types.name: HoverCardProfileProps
types.doc: A person preview for `HoverCard`: portrait, name, role, a short bio, a couple of numbers, and a quiet footer line. Its rows settle in with a tiny stagger.

members.name: role
members.doc: Role and team, such as "Product designer, Payments".

members.name: avatar
members.doc: A portrait URL, or your own image element such as next/image. Initials show when it is missing.

members.name: meta
members.doc: A footer line, such as a location and local time.

components.name: ResizablePanel
components.doc: Carries a pane's configuration into `ResizablePanels`. Rendered on its own it shows its children unchanged.

types.name: ResizablePanelProps
types.doc: One pane of a `ResizablePanels` group. It only carries configuration; the group renders it.

members.name: id
members.doc: Stable id, also used by the dividers' `aria-controls`.

members.name: label
members.doc: Names the pane for its divider, for example "Folders".

members.name: defaultSize
members.doc: Starting share of the group. Shares are relative, so they need not add up to 100.

members.name: minSize
members.doc: Width in px where the pane starts to resist. Its content never reflows below it; it clips and fades instead.

members.name: collapsible
members.doc: Dragging well past the minimum, or flicking toward the edge, snaps the pane closed. Its divider then shows a restore tab.

types.name: ResizablePanelsProps
types.doc: A horizontal split view whose panes people resize by dragging the dividers between them, the way a mail or code editor window works. Use it when people need to trade space between side-by-side content for the task at hand. Dividers follow the pointer 1:1, resist past a pane's limits, and snap collapsible panes closed. Each divider is a focusable separator: arrows resize, Home and End jump to the limits, Enter hides or restores a collapsible pane, and a double-click resets the layout. The group needs a definite height.

members.name: label
members.doc: Names the group for assistive technology.

members.name: children
members.doc: `ResizablePanel` elements, in order. The set of panes should stay the same for the life of the group.

members.name: onLayoutChange
members.doc: Called with each pane's share in percent after a resize settles.

components.name: ToastStackProvider
components.doc: Scopes a toast queue to its subtree, so two stacks on one page never share toasts.

members.name: onClick
members.doc: Runs the action. The toast closes afterwards unless the handler updates it, so an Undo can morph the toast into its result.

members.name: id
members.doc: Reuse an id to update a toast in place instead of stacking a new one.

members.name: duration
members.doc: Milliseconds before the toast closes itself. Defaults by type; loading toasts wait for an update. Pass Infinity to keep it until closed.

members.name: toast
members.doc: Shows a toast and returns its id.

members.name: update
members.doc: Morphs a toast in place: icon, copy, and height animate to the new content and its timer restarts. Pass `action: undefined` to remove the action.

members.name: dismiss
members.doc: Dismisses one toast, or every toast when called without an id.

members.name: duration
members.doc: Base lifetime in milliseconds. Warnings and errors stay 1.6 times longer.

members.name: limit
members.doc: Oldest toasts beyond this count are dropped from the queue.

types.name: ToastStackProps
types.doc: The viewport for a toast stack. Render it once inside a `ToastStackProvider` and call `useToastStack()` anywhere below. Use it for short, non-blocking results of what someone just did: new toasts rise from the bottom edge, older ones tuck behind, and hovering or focusing the stack fans it out into a list. Toasts pause while the stack is open or the tab is hidden, and swipe right to dismiss.

members.name: label
members.doc: Accessible name of the notification region.

members.name: contained
members.doc: Pins the stack inside the nearest positioned ancestor instead of the window, for panels and previews.

members.name: visibleToasts
members.doc: How many toasts show at once. Older ones wait behind and return as the front ones close.

members.name: hotkey
members.doc: Alt+T moves focus into the stack.

members.name: id
members.doc: Stable identity. Keep it the same while the value changes, so the segment re-flows instead of being replaced.

types.name: UsageMeterProps
types.doc: Use a usage meter for a fixed allowance, such as storage or seats, when people need to see what takes the space and how close they are to the limit.

members.name: label
members.doc: What is measured, such as "Workspace storage".

members.name: segments
members.doc: Used amounts in display order. Up to four read clearly.

members.name: limit
members.doc: The plan limit, in the same unit as the segments.

members.name: decimals
members.doc: Digits after the decimal point.

members.name: warnAt
members.doc: Share of the limit at which the meter warns that it is almost full.

members.name: actionLabel
members.doc: Label of the button that does the step. Without it, the step is checked off by hand.

members.name: onAction
members.doc: Runs the step. Resolve to check it off; throw an Error to keep it open and show the error's message.

types.name: OnboardingChecklistProps
types.doc: A getting started checklist for a new account or workspace. The ring and count follow every check, finished steps strike through and fold into a completed row that opens again, and the next step opens and takes focus. Use it for a short, one time setup of three to eight steps; use a step form when the order is strict.

members.name: doneTitle
members.doc: Title once every step is done.

components.name: ImageCompare
components.doc: Before and after, split by a divider. Drag anywhere to move it: the handle follows 1:1, rubber-bands past the edges, and stays where it is released. A press on the image springs the divider there; on touch the press waits to see a sideways drag so the page still scrolls. Arrow keys step 1% (Shift for 10%), Home and End reveal one side fully, and a double-click on the handle springs it back to the middle.

members.name: before
members.doc: The original, shown on the left (or top). Pass an image with its own alt text; it is sized to cover the frame.

members.name: after
members.doc: The result, shown on the right (or bottom).

members.name: position
members.doc: Where the divider sits, in percent from the left (or top).

members.name: orientation
members.doc: Vertical stacks the images top and bottom. Changing it swings the divider a quarter turn instead of swapping layouts.

members.name: labels
members.doc: Captions over each side. They fade as the divider reaches them. Pass false to hide them.

members.name: label
members.doc: Accessible name of the divider.

members.name: aspectRatio
members.doc: Frame proportions, as a CSS aspect-ratio.

types.name: CarouselProps
types.doc: A row of slides people browse by dragging, flicking, a trackpad swipe, the arrow keys, or the controls below it. Use it for a short, ordered set of peers such as products or case studies, where the neighbours stay in view as a hint that there is more. The active slide sits in the center, its neighbours shrink and dim with distance, and the page indicator stretches into a pill that travels with the slides frame by frame.

members.name: label
members.doc: Names the carousel for assistive technology, for example "From the Harbour suites".

members.name: children
members.doc: One child per slide.

members.name: index
members.doc: Controlled active slide. Pair with `onIndexChange`.

members.name: slideSize
members.doc: Width of one slide as a CSS length. Use `cqw` for a share of the carousel width.

members.name: slideLabel
members.doc: Names each slide and its indicator. Defaults to "2 of 5".

members.name: autoplay
members.doc: Starts rotating on mount. Off by default, so motion begins with the viewer.

types.name: CardStackProps
types.doc: A deck of cards reviewed one at a time: drag or flick the top card left or right, or use the buttons and arrow keys. Use it for quick, one-by-one triage where each item deserves a moment of attention: shortlisting destinations, candidates, or design options. Use a list or table when people need to compare items side by side.

members.name: getLabel
members.doc: A short name for the card, used in its accessible label and announcements, such as "Lisbon".

members.name: labels
members.doc: Action names for each side, used on the buttons and the stamps that appear while dragging.

members.name: outcomes
members.doc: Past tense of each action for announcements, such as "skipped" and "shortlisted".

members.name: label
members.doc: Accessible name for the stack.

members.name: renderEmpty
members.doc: Shown once every card has been decided. Receives a function that brings all cards back.

members.name: label

members.name: axisLabel

members.name: headingLevel

components.name: PresenceDot

types.name: ToastActionCloseReason
types.doc: Why the toast closed: the countdown ran out, the person closed it (button, Escape or swipe), or the action was taken.

types.name: ToastActionPosition
types.doc: `inline` renders where it is placed, like `Toast`. The others pin it to the bottom edge, like `ToastStack`.

types.name: ToastActionProps
types.doc: A toast with one action and a visible deadline. Use it right after something reversible (delete, archive, send): a thin bar drains until the toast leaves by itself, hovering or focusing the toast holds the countdown, and taking the action swaps the copy for a short confirmation before it leaves. For a plain confirmation use `Toast`; for several at once use `ToastStack`.

members.name: title
members.doc: What just happened, in a few words. Changing the title or description while the toast is open swaps the copy in place and restarts the countdown.

members.name: description
members.doc: Optional second line with the detail.

members.name: resetKey
members.doc: Identifies the event the toast is about. A new value while the toast is open starts it over (action back, countdown full) even when the copy is the same, for example when the same file is deleted twice.

members.name: icon
members.doc: Glyph in the status circle before the action is taken, for example a trash icon at 16px.

members.name: actionLabel
members.doc: Label of the single action.

members.name: onAction
members.doc: Runs when the action is taken. The toast then shows the confirmation and leaves by itself.

members.name: confirmation
members.doc: Title shown after the action is taken.

members.name: confirmationDescription
members.doc: Optional second line of the confirmation.

members.name: confirmationDuration
members.doc: Milliseconds the confirmation stays before the toast leaves.

members.name: open
members.doc: Whether the toast is showing (controlled).

members.name: defaultOpen
members.doc: Whether the toast starts showing when `open` is not passed.

members.name: onOpenChange
members.doc: Called when the toast closes itself, with the reason: `"timeout"`, `"dismiss"`, or `"action"` whenever the action was taken first.

members.name: duration
members.doc: Milliseconds of countdown before the toast closes itself. Pass 0 or Infinity to keep it until it is closed; the bar is then hidden.

members.name: position
members.doc: Where the toast sits. `inline` stays in the flow; the bottom positions pin it to the window.

members.name: contained
members.doc: With a bottom position, pins the toast inside the nearest positioned ancestor instead of the window, for panels and previews.

While it runs, a bar and a number advance; when it ends, the same toast morphs in place: the bar completes and folds away, the spinner becomes a drawn check and the copy swaps, or, on failure, the bar freezes in the danger tone and a Retry action appears. The chart outside the window fades back; inside, a floating lens with a thick bezel replays the selected slice at full color, cropped 1:1 out of the plot. components.name: AvatarUpload
components.doc: Click or drop a photo onto the avatar to crop it in place with drag, pinch and zoom. It uploads through a progress ring and settles, with clear errors and retry. Phases: idle -> crop -> uploading -> (idle with the new photo | failed with retry/discard). A removed avatar shows its initials. The crop drags with a rubber band past its bounds, zooms toward the pointer, and exports a circular 512 px image (PNG for PNG input, JPEG q92 otherwise).

types.name: AvatarUploadErrorCode
types.doc: Reasons a chosen file can be rejected before it reaches the uploader.

members.name: message
members.doc: The message the component is showing, so a host can mirror it elsewhere.

members.name: open
members.doc: Opens the native file picker.

members.name: selectFile
members.doc: Validates and takes a file the same way a picked one is treated (type, size, decode).

members.name: name

members.name: src
members.doc: Current photo. Omit (or pass null) to start with initials.

members.name: onUpload
members.type: ( image: Blob, options: { report: (progress: number) => void; signal: AbortSignal; original: File }, ) => Promise<string | void>
members.doc: Uploads the cropped result (PNG stays PNG, everything else exports as JPEG). Resolving with a URL makes it the new photo; resolving void uses the exported image itself. Rejecting lands on the retry state, aborting via `signal` cancels silently back to the previous photo.

members.name: onError

members.name: size

members.name: outputSize

components.name: HeroContent

components.name: HeroLumen
components.doc: Centered hero, one full screen: a headline over a drifting mesh, and a live revenue dashboard rising from the bottom edge. The window settles from a tilt as it enters and runs off the bottom of the screen into a fade. It is real markup built from ryan-ui charts; its range control works.

components.name: HeroRelay
components.doc: Split hero, one full screen: the copy beside a live workflow graph on a dotted canvas. Sample Stripe events arrive on their own and run the workflow node by node; the data draws along each edge, the branch decides which actions run, and every step reports its time. "Send test event" runs the next sample at once. The run pauses off screen, and under reduced motion each event shows its finished run without playing.

components.name: HeroCadence
components.doc: Minimal hero, one full screen: large type over a slowly drifting mesh gradient with grain, and the teams that use the product along the bottom edge.
